run_by: Claude (weight-research-fable): the solver, the sweep and the execution (code/signal-trace/pipeline/weight_edit/tube.py). The objective, the bounds and the acceptance are Astra's (weight-research-astra), in records/retrospectives/2026-11-10-stable-training-review-astra.md.

recorder_revision.why: The original recordings were made with the recorder at commit fbdaa861; today's recorder (commit 76134ea7) differs from it in its source by one twelve-line filter, stream_labels, which a case has to ask for. Answers with nothing supplied do not ask for it, so both programs read them the same way. Astra reviewed the source and ruled that today's recorder is kept for the original file's second answers, for this pair of programs and this unfiltered path only (records/retrospectives/2026-11-10-stable-training-review-astra.md, 'Recorder revision decision').

hypothesis: A capability leaves a recurring difference between the traces of correct and wrong answers, from where the two shared patterns part until they reconcile, and editing the weights where that difference lives repairs the capability. In the form this run tests: if each matrix is changed only as far as it brings the wrong answers' pattern toward the correct one where the two diverge, while every other part of the trace stays inside what the original model's own answers vary by, then the edited model, answering on its own, carries the wrong group's trace nearer the correct pattern over the divergence and leaves both groups' patterns, their spread, the questions' positions and the size of the state where the original model has them.
what_went_wrong_before: The four rungs of November 10 (a2-path, b2-path, c2-path with c2-protected, d2-path) built the edit at full strength and added protection afterwards, and none shows what the round has to show. a2-path moved its own traces 0.79 of the way along the gap over places 142 to 313 and about one gap to the side in both groups, completed 17 of the 30 wrong answers and broke 12 of the 30 correct ones. b2-path held the broken answers' rows on their given text and 4 of the 12 stayed complete: the model's own answers leave that text at the fourth token. c2-path and d2-path ended with 12 and 7 of the wrong answers complete. Four causes are on record. (1) Nothing bounded what moved where nothing was asked: the side movement was as large as the move. (2) The strength of each change was chosen by how much of the ask it met on the wrong answers' given text; nothing in that choice saw what the change did anywhere else. (3) The model file keeps a weight to about one part in 256, so a small change was mostly not written and the rest went in as whole steps: the same solve at layer 3's attention leaves 0.985 of the divergence in the file's format and 0.636 as float32 (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/path-bf16.jsonl, path-float32.jsonl). (4) A pass that reads an answer as given text is not the computation the model answers in: reading several tokens at once the engine rounds what goes into each matrix first, and the merge lies 0.0001 to 0.0007 from what the same weights give one token at a time (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/operator_cpu.out). Beside these, the rungs were judged by what the answers said, which Marcos set aside on November 10: the judge is the computational trace.
why_this_direction: Marcos, November 10 (journal/2026-11-10-controlled-training.md): protection is part of the training, not a later rung; where the traces already overlap the values are not changed or minimally changed; success is judged by the computational trace, not by the model writing the expected result; no subjectivity in the numbers; a sample of the capability's trace is enough, the model does not have to read all 60 answers; and no step waits on another for its own sake. Steps 5 and 6 of the method were rewritten from those words and the training was designed with Astra on stored rows of the original model only. What those rows can say is said: with the matrices as float32 and the bounds from the original answers' own variance, every one of the 70 matrices, changed by itself from the unchanged model, moves the fitting answers' wrong pattern toward the correct one inside every bound (0.45 to 0.96 of the tube loss left, median 0.77), and the answers no fit used follow within 0.002 to 0.031 (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/map-float32.jsonl). What they cannot say is the training itself: each matrix on what arrives once the earlier changes are in the model, the engine's own output of each written merge, the bounds once their floors are measured by a pass through the original file, and above all the edited model's own answers. Only a run through the model reads those, so the next step of the method is the first sweep, declared here before it runs. It is one sweep and not a search: nothing in it is tuned to a result, and what it finds decides whether a second sweep starts from it (step 6).
repeating_pattern_check: What has happened more than once, why, and what this run does about each. (a) An edit moved the trace where nothing was asked, in every rung: nothing held those parts while a matrix was solved. Here every part of the trace has a bound from the original answers' own variance and every step of every solve is cut where a bound would be left. (b) A reading during the build did not predict the model's own answers, four times: the rows read were the wrong answers' own, on given text. Here the fitting answers are in three groups, a change is solved on one, held by the second and read on the third within that solve; the third affects stopping/selection, and across rotations every fitting member participates in construction. Half of the answers enter no fit, but their repeated development readings are not untouched independent confirmation; every pass feeds the answer's own tokens one at a time; and the test is the model's own answers, read by the trace alone. (c) The strength of an edit was a number taken or tuned (full strength, a ridge chosen by the ask alone, a floor from eight requests). Here no strength is chosen: a change stops where a bound or a read group stops it. (d) A result was read off the answers' text and the trace came second; Marcos corrected this more than once. Here no text, token or score enters any verdict, and what the answers say is reported beside the verdicts without deciding anything. (e) This session reacted to a rung's numbers by building the next rung. This run is not an answer to a number: it is the first run of the training Marcos asked for, and its prediction is written before it. (f) In the development map itself, something already repeats: 23 of the 70 matrices, each changed alone, leave 1 to 14 of their 960 direction cells over the bound on the answers no fit used, up to 1.55 of the bound, at the tightest asked cells, while the fitting answers hold. That is the same split between fitted and unfitted rows as (b), now small and measured. The run does not widen a bound for it: Astra's ruling keeps the replay's limits as they are, and the replay on the unused half says whether these cells stay, grow or wash out in the composed model.

rule.members: The 60 registered answers of the overlap, 30 correct and 30 wrong (first incorrect calculation: the descent subtracted), with every generated step and every question position: 30,546 answer steps and 10,319 question rows. The fitting answers are every other answer of each group in the answers' own order, 15 and 15, in three groups of 5 and 5; the other 15 and 15 enter no fit. The patterns and all reference variances come from the original 30 and 30. Replay allowances use the reference count 30; native own-generation mean budgets use the evaluated count, 15 per group in the deciding cohort.
rule.model: A copy of the original file with the 70 attention-output and feed-forward-down matrices stored as float32, the same values bit for bit, read back against the original before use. Every movement is counted from the original BF16 file; what the copy's format moves by itself is part of the movement counted and is no allowance.
rule.target: At each matrix's merge, where the two original patterns of the state's direction lie further apart than two halves of one group do (gap > 2 chance), the wrong group's mean state is asked to move to the nearest point of the ball around the correct pattern whose radius is sqrt(2 chance). Inside the ball, and where the patterns follow each other, nothing is asked. The tube loss is the squared distance still outside the ball, summed over the asked places.
rule.bounds: At each place of the axis and each merge, for each group: the mean over its members of the squared movement of the unit state (the wrong group's after taking out their shared movement along the gap where a move is asked), and the same for the log of the state's size; for each question, the mean squared movement over its prompt positions, state and size. Each is held to the variance of the original group's members there over their number, 30, and never to less than how far this run's own reading of the original file lies from the recorded rows.
rule.fit: One matrix at a time, on the model's own expression of the merge with the learned scale and both projections inside. A step is first-order through the merge; every bounded part pushes back with a strength that grows as it nears its bound; after the step the change is put through the merge itself as the file would keep it, every row's movement is measured, and the part of the step that keeps every bound is found by halving. While a bound is outside, nothing pulls: the steps only bring it back.
rule.choose: Which change of a matrix is kept is decided inside the fitting answers. In turn one group is solved on, one must keep its bounds at every step, one is only read after each step. The three solves go in step along one path of ridges that starts at the matrix's own unit and is halved stage by stage, each solve starting a stage from where its last ended. The path ends with the stage in which a read group, or all the fitting answers together, leaves a bound. Of the stages before it the one whose three ends leave their read groups the least tube loss, the worst of the three first, is kept, and the change is the mean of its three ends if that holds every bound on every group and on all together, otherwise the one end that does and leaves the least. Nothing is changed unless less tube loss is left than the matrix as it stands leaves.
rule.sweep: The 70 matrices in path order (layer 0 attention, layer 0 feed-forward, layer 1 attention, and so on), each solved on what arrives with the earlier changes in the model, read by a pass through the model with the fitting answers' own tokens fed one at a time. The same pass reads what the engine itself puts out at the merges just above, which no later matrix can move. If a bound is outside there, or nothing brings this matrix's own merge back inside, the change of the matrix written just before is taken back by halves until it holds. Where nothing can be taken back, or no part holds, the sweep ends there and is not accepted; the model is kept as it stands for inspection.
rule.replay: The finished model read once on the 15 and 15 answers no fit used, their own tokens fed one at a time, at all 105 merges from the engine's own output, counted from the original file's. The replay passes if every bound holds at every merge and the tube loss, summed over the merges, is less than the unedited float32 copy's by the same reference. Nothing is chosen from it.
rule.own_answers: The test. The original file, the unedited copy and the finished model each answer the 60 questions with nothing supplied, greedy, to the limit the recordings were made with. Each answer is laid on the frozen axis by its computation alone and read at all 105 merges: the tube on the wrong pattern; for each group at each place and merge how far its pattern moved and how far the spread of its members around the original centre changed, for the state and for its size; each question's prompt rows. Each of the four is held to twice the original answers' variance of that quantity over the number of answers in the mean read, 15 a group on the answers no fit used, which decide, and never to less than what the original file's second set of answers reads against its first. The own answers hold if every answer ended by itself, every budget and prompt bound holds at every merge, and the tube loss is less than the unedited copy's own answers'. No text, token or score enters.
rule.verdict: The replay and the own answers are two verdicts, read in either order, and stay two (Astra, November 10, 'Replay decision after ordering removal' in records/retrospectives/2026-11-10-stable-training-review-astra.md). The sweep is eligible for a next one when both hold for the same model, the same frozen reference and the same answers. The own answers holding while the replay fails is a finding about the model's own traces with the failed replay beside it; it is not an eligible sweep and it does not show the answers were damaged. The repair of the pattern is whole only if, beyond that, no asked place is left outside its ball. This is a statement about the recurring pattern of the trace on these answers, not that every answer is right.
rule.what_is_frozen: The reference (patterns, bounds, floors) is written once from the original model's recordings and this run's reading of the original file, before any matrix is written, and only read after. The budgets of the own answers and their floors are written once from the original file's two sets of answers, with their sha256, and checked at the reading. A reading of the model before any change is made through the original file or through a copy read back value for value equal to it, whenever it is made.
rule.what_only_bounds_the_work: Five layers to a pass and ten answers to a capture only bound the raw stream on disk; the rows read are the same however they are grouped. The solver's caps and spacing are parameters below.
rule.what_a_rerun_would_repeat: The stored-row procedure did not reproduce exactly between the recorded executions, and a stage of the path ends on a threshold. Floating-point reduction variability is a plausible mechanism, but these comparisons do not isolate its exact source. Two runs of the same solve on stored rows left layer 15's attention 0.4511 and 0.4508 of its tube loss, and ended one stage apart at layer 8's attention, 0.637 and 0.706, each inside every bound on the fitting answers (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/map-float32.jsonl and solver-numbers.jsonl). A second run of this sweep would hold the same bounds and need not keep the same stage at every matrix: what the run shows is one outcome of the procedure.
rule.beside_the_verdicts: What the three models write to the 60 questions is scored as in the round's scoring and reported beside the verdicts; it decides nothing (Marcos, November 10). Reserved-40b stays sealed.

asked.derivation: gap > 2 * chance at a place and merge, where gap is squared pattern distance and chance = V_correct/30 + V_wrong/30. For either original group g, two complementary 15-member halves have expected squared mean contrast 4*V_g/30. Averaging that contrast scale across the two groups gives 2*chance. This is the frozen reference-resolution policy for asking a move, not a significance test or proof that a smaller discrepancy is absent.
asked.scales_with: the number of members in each group and their spread at that place and merge

ball.derivation: radius sqrt(2 * chance) around the correct pattern at each asked place and merge. Its squared radius is the average complementary-half contrast scale of the correct and wrong original groups, not the correct group's variance alone and not the expected distance itself. The nearest point of this ball is the declared target-resolution policy; it is not a confidence region for the correct centre.
ball.scales_with: the number of members in each group and their spread at that place and merge

bound.derivation: For each group, place and merge: the sample variance over the group's 30 members of the member's mean unit state there, summed over the coordinates, divided by 30; the same for the mean log size. The variance-over-count is an estimated group-mean variation scale used here as a conservative engineering allowance for same-history row-squared movement. It is not a confidence interval, a calibrated test of that row statistic, or proof that a movement below it is indistinguishable from sampling. For a question: at every place of the prompt the variance of its group's questions over 30, and over the question's positions the mean of that (Astra, records/retrospectives/2026-11-10-stable-training-review-astra.md).
bound.scales_with: the number of members in each group and their spread at that place and merge

reading_floor.derivation: No bound is less than what the readings themselves resolve, measured as the bound is, squares first: how far this run's pass through the original file (baseline-original) lies from the rows recorded while the original model generated; for the size, how far the file's expression of the merge lies from the size the engine recorded; at the last layer's last merge, where no prompt row was recorded, how far two readings of the prompts through the original file lie apart. Each bound is the larger of its variance term and this. It is measured from the original file only: the copy's and the edited model's noise widen nothing.
reading_floor.scales_with: the engine build, the card and how a pass reads; measured again for another model or machine

fitting_half.derivation: Every other answer of each group in the answers' own order, 15 of 30. With n answers fitted and 30 - n only read, the sampling variance of what each side shows goes as 1/n and 1/(30 - n); the larger of the two is least at n = 15. The order is the registration's own, fixed before any fit.
fitting_half.scales_with: the number of members in each group

three_groups.derivation: Every third of the fitting answers within each group, 5 and 5 each. A change is solved on answers, held by other answers and read on answers no step used: three roles that must not share an answer need three groups, three is the least number that gives each role its own, and equal sizes by the same argument as the half. Each group takes each role once.
three_groups.scales_with: the number of fitting answers in each group

ridge_unit.derivation: Where the path of ridges starts, per matrix: the mean, over the directions a change can take, of the bounds' own push-back on the fitting rows before anything has moved, with each place's strength set so that every place at its bound costs as much as every ask unmet (the original tube loss over twice the number of places). Computed from the matrix's rows at the time it is solved; it places the path, and where the path ends is decided by the bounds and the read groups.
ridge_unit.scales_with: the matrix, its rows after the earlier changes, the bounds and the tube loss at its merge

own_budget.derivation: For each group, place and merge and each of the four quantities (the pattern's direction, its log size, the spread of the members' directions around the original centre, the spread of their log sizes): twice the original 30 answers' sample variance of that quantity over the number of answers in the mean that is read, 15 a group on the answers no fit used. The factor two and count 15 give the reference scale of a contrast between complementary original 15-member halves (or equally sized independent-reference means). They do not claim that the actual paired E/O contrast has variance 2V/15: that contrast also depends on E's variance and E/O covariance. This is a frozen reference-resolution policy, not a confidence guarantee. A model that words an answer differently is not held row by row: another answer of the same group lies about 60 times a row's replay bound away with both patterns unchanged (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/own-check-rows.out; the check of this budget is own-check.out beside it).
own_budget.scales_with: the number of answers in the mean read and the original answers' spread of each quantity

own_floor.derivation: No budget is less than what the original file does not repeat: the same four quantities read on a second set of the original BF16 file's own answers to the same questions against the recordings, on the same cohort and through the same registration (own/original, own/original-floors.npz). Made only if every one of those answers ended by itself and the capture was made as the recordings were; never from the copy or the edited model.
own_floor.scales_with: the engine build, the card and the recorder; measured again for another model or machine

answer_limit.derivation: 768 tokens, the limit every one of the 60 original recordings was made with (max_tokens there). An answer that runs into it is not a whole answer, and nothing is counted from a set that has one.
answer_limit.scales_with: the limit of the recordings the answers are compared with

resolved.derivation: sqrt of float32's epsilon, approximately 0.000345: the relative linear-residual stopping tolerance, the minimum remaining-bound fraction in the barrier weights, and the lowest relative ridge visited. Computing this value from epsilon does not derive the square-root choice from model evidence or prove that smaller remainders are numerically unresolvable. This is a numerical setting with an explicit calibration gap, not a trace allowance or an intrinsic float32 accuracy floor; its roles must not be conflated with the independently checked feasibility bounds.
resolved.scales_with: the arithmetic the rows are recorded and solved in

iterations_of_a_linear_solve.derivation: 40. A cap on the solver's work that turned out not to be without effect, so its effect is stated. Every linear solve on record runs to it. Of the caps tried (20, 40, 80, 160), 40 is the least at which the stage kept is the one kept at 160: layer 15's attention keeps ridge 2^-3 at 20 and 2^-4 at 40, 80 and 160; layer 3's attention keeps 2^-6 at all four. What the cap still moves at 40 and above is the tube loss left inside that stage: 0.4508, 0.4473, 0.4438 at 40, 80, 160 at layer 15's attention and 0.5406, 0.5390, 0.5390 at layer 3's, at most 0.007, against 0.07 between two neighbouring stages (layer 8's attention, below) and 0.03 by which the unused answers trail. A solve cut short is a smaller step, never a step outside a bound: what is inside is read from the merge at the written weights. At 160 a solve takes 2.6 to 5 times as long. Still queued behind another project's lease on the card when this was declared: layer 10's feed-forward at 20, 80 and 160 iterations, layers 15 and 3 attention with the ridge quartered from stage to stage, and layer 15's attention with the bracket eight times wider and eight times narrower. They are read before the build starts; if one of them keeps another stage than the declared numbers do, the number is revised here before the build, with the row.
iterations_of_a_linear_solve.scales_with: the matrix's width and how unevenly its rows weigh on a change; measured again for another model

rounds_of_a_stage.derivation: 40. A cap on the solver's work, not derived from the traces: a solve of a stage ends when a step gains nothing, and after at most 40 rounds it hands where it stands to the next stage, which starts from there. In the map 846 solves took a median of 4 rounds and 11 at the 95th percentile; 4 reached 40 (layers 28 and 31 attention), none of them in the stage that was kept. Its effect on those two matrices at a higher cap is not measured.
rounds_of_a_stage.scales_with: how slowly a matrix's solves gain near their bounds

spacing_of_the_ridges.derivation: The ridge is halved from one stage to the next. The factor only spaces the stages tried along one path, and one stage is the resolution of what is kept: the map's matrices keep ridges from 2^-6 to 2^8 of their unit, and two neighbouring stages differ by 0.07 of the tube loss at layer 8's attention (0.706 left at 2^-5, 0.637 at 2^-6, in two runs of the same solve, records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/solver-numbers.jsonl beside the map). Because a stage ends on a threshold, that resolution is also what a rerun may differ by (rule, what_a_rerun_would_repeat). Still queued behind another project's lease on the card when this was declared: layer 10's feed-forward at 20, 80 and 160 iterations, layers 15 and 3 attention with the ridge quartered from stage to stage, and layer 15's attention with the bracket eight times wider and eight times narrower. They are read before the build starts; if one of them keeps another stage than the declared numbers do, the number is revised here before the build, with the row.
spacing_of_the_ridges.scales_with: nothing in the traces; a finer spacing costs a stage's solves for every stage added

bracket.derivation: How closely the part of a step that holds every bound is bracketed by halving: to sqrt of float32's epsilon, the same tolerance as the linear solve's. This is a chosen line-search resolution, not a minimum distinguishable float32 step: representability depends on the matrix values and update direction. It can change how much of a step is retained. Feasibility is separately evaluated through the implemented merge at the stored weights and ultimately through native readings; it is not an exact-real-arithmetic guarantee. Still queued behind another project's lease on the card when this was declared: layer 10's feed-forward at 20, 80 and 160 iterations, layers 15 and 3 attention with the ridge quartered from stage to stage, and layer 15's attention with the bracket eight times wider and eight times narrower. They are read before the build starts; if one of them keeps another stage than the declared numbers do, the number is revised here before the build, with the row.
bracket.scales_with: the arithmetic the change is written in

prediction.expected_observation: From the development map, with what it cannot say. The unedited float32 copy: expected to hold every bound against the original file at every merge, because the values are the same and, one token at a time on the CPU, the float32 product of those values equals the engine's recorded output (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/operator_cpu.out). The card runs float32 matrices through another kernel, which no record has read against a bound, so this is a prediction and not a known; if the copy is outside somewhere, the first matrices there only bring it back, and that is reported as found. The build: every matrix that is written holds every bound on the fitting answers, by construction, or the sweep ends there. Alone from the unchanged model every one of the 70 matrices changed and left the fitting answers 0.45 to 0.96 of the tube loss at its own merge, median 0.77. The state carries a change of an earlier merge into every later one, so in the sweep a matrix finds part of its ask already met and part of its bounds already used: some matrices may be left as they stand, and, summed over the 105 merges, the fitting answers are left less than 0.77 of the original tube loss. Changes may be taken back by halves, since each written merge is read again from the engine's own output, which a solve does not see. The replay on the answers no fit used: their tube loss follows the fitting answers' within a few hundredths at each merge (the map: 0.002 to 0.031 behind), so it is less than the copy's. But alone, 23 of the 70 matrices leave 1 to 14 of their 960 direction cells over the bound on those answers, up to 1.55 of it, the detailed layers 15 and 17 attention reruns place their 24 exceedances in the wrong group at asked places 169 to 192, with fitting ratios about 0.73 to 0.91. That localization does not cover all failures: layer 20 feed-forward has four correct-group direction cells at places 255 to 258 (1.046 to 1.253, fitting 0.436 to 0.489), layer 25 feed-forward has a correct-group cell at place 245 (1.053, fitting 0.839), and the layer 3 attention size cell at place 151 has a fitting ratio about 0.006 at 40 iterations despite a reading ratio 1.449. Some out-of-bound cells are expected in the composed model, so under the limits as they are the replay is expected NOT to pass on every bound. The own answers: the wrong group's pattern moves toward the correct one where a move is asked, so the tube loss on the answers no fit used is below the copy's own answers' and below what the original file's second answers read; the correct group's pattern, both groups' spread, the sizes and the prompts stay inside their budgets at most merges, and a budget that is left is left where the original answers barely vary. Whether every budget holds at all 105 merges is not predicted: no record so far reads an edited model's own answers under this rule.
prediction.failures_only: Per merge and family, every cell outside its bound or budget with its size, group, place and whether a move is asked there, for the replay and for the own answers; every matrix taken back or left unchanged with why; every answer that ran into the limit. Per wrong answer, its fields before and after and where its own trace lies against the two patterns, beside the verdicts.

would_weaken_it: The hypothesis: the edited model's own answers carry the wrong group's trace into the correct pattern's resolution over the divergence with every budget held, and what those answers write is no nearer the correct calculation. By Marcos's direction that does not judge the training, but it would say the recurring difference in the trace is not what carries the capability. The construction, not the hypothesis: the sweep ends outside a bound within the first layers; or the replay's tube loss on the unused answers is not less than the copy's although the fitting answers' is; or the own answers' tube loss is not below the copy's, or not below what the original file's second answers read with nothing changed; or the own answers move as far to the side as along the gap again. Any of these means the bounds as built do not carry from the fitted rows to the model's own computation, and the run then does not test the hypothesis. The unedited copy lying outside a bound by itself would weaken neither: it would say the format is not a free change and has to be counted, which the run does.

revisions.stage: After the first command had begun; no build.jsonl existed when these corrections were recorded.
revisions.reason: Acceptance-side review of the declared interpretation and the existing development records.
revisions.changed: Correct the false all-wrong-group localization; distinguish the two-group half-contrast radius from correct-group-only variability; label replay and own-generation normalization as reference policies rather than confidence guarantees; distinguish observed rerun variation from an isolated hardware cause; identify sqrt(epsilon) as a numerical setting with an unresolved calibration rationale; state the data-dependent roles of the fitting thirds.
revisions.unchanged: No numerical value, bound, floor, cohort, prediction of replay failure, model input, command or running process changed. The original declaration remains in commit ab92ead8.
